title: Git ref and artifact object enumeration capabilities
description:
Objective: add the two ABSENT enumeration capabilities that the recovery-window inventory adapters must call, to the shipped observers/stores that already own those boundaries. This is a prerequisite production task created because the capability is missing, NOT a narrowed DoD and NOT a test-owned reimplementation.

MEASURED GAP at 2026-08-09 by architect-d46fcb95, symbol by symbol:
- `GitObserver` (packages/runner/src/scope/scope-contract.ts) declares exactly headCommit(), statusPorcelainV2(), lsFilesTracked(), lsFilesIgnored(), submodulePaths(). There is NO branch or ref enumeration. `grep -rn "for-each-ref|show-ref|--branches|refs/heads|listRefs" packages/runner/src --include=*.ts` (non-test) returns ZERO.
- `ArtifactStore` (packages/runner/src/artifacts/artifact-contract.ts) declares exactly stageArtifact(), verifyArtifact(), deleteArtifact(); `ArtifactFsPort` declares openWrite/write/fsync/close/exists/rename/persistAfterRename/readAll/unlink. There is NO directory listing. `grep -rn "readdir|listObjects|listStaging|scandir" packages/runner/src` returns ZERO outside runtime-entrypoint.test.ts.

Consequently task-0325dcf7ee744123b40cf583230c7b6a's DoD 2 ("Git branches/refs ... artifact objects/staging") currently has nothing to call.

Deliverable, additive only:
1. Extend GitObserver with a bounded ref enumeration (refs with their target commit, covering refs/heads and refs/remotes) implemented in createNodeGitObserver via the existing hermetic runGit helper — same shell:false / bounded maxBuffer / timeout / windowsHide discipline, NUL-framed output, and the existing ScopeObserverError codes for overflow and malformed output. Do not loosen hermeticGitEnvironment.
2. Extend ArtifactFsPort with a bounded directory listing and ArtifactStore with object/staging enumeration over the store's own `<root>/objects/<sha256>` layout, implemented in createNodeArtifactFs / createArtifactStore. An entry whose name is not a valid content address is reported as such, never skipped silently.

Both additions are ENUMERATION ONLY: no new mutation, no new authority, no change to any existing method's behaviour or refusal codes.

NOT in scope: the recovery-inventory contract, coverage protocol, or any inventory adapter (those are task-0325dcf7's children); scheduler rows; deciding adopt/quarantine.

Owned paths: packages/runner/src/scope/scope-contract.ts, packages/runner/src/scope/scope-git.ts, packages/runner/src/artifacts/artifact-contract.ts, packages/runner/src/artifacts/artifact-node-fs.ts, packages/runner/src/artifacts/artifact-store.ts, their focused tests, and the minimal @moe/runner root export wiring.

WARNING measured by the architect: packages/runner/src/index-surface.test.ts pins the EXACT root namespace against a hand-written EXPECTED_EXPORTS list plus a hard-coded `expect(EXPECTED_EXPORTS.length).toBe(116)`. Any new root value export reddens it until transcribed and the count bumped. That file was ALREADY red at 2026-08-09 from an unrelated in-flight task's exports; capture the baseline before editing and attribute per the project's path-attributed-baseline rail.

Consumer (global rail Clause 1): task-0325dcf7ee744123b40cf583230c7b6a's Git/integration and artifact/staging adapter child.

Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/runner test
definitionOfDone: GitObserver declares a bounded ref enumeration and createNodeGitObserver implements it through the existing hermetic runGit helper with shell:false, bounded maxBuffer, explicit timeout and windowsHide, returning each ref with its target commit; hermeticGitEnvironment is unchanged.

ArtifactFsPort declares a bounded directory listing and ArtifactStore exposes object/staging enumeration over its own <root>/objects/<sha256> layout; an entry whose name is not a valid content address is reported with a stable code, never silently skipped.

Overflow, a malformed or truncated git response, an absent directory, and an unreadable entry each refuse with an existing stable code and the layer that refused; a test pins the exact code and layer for every one, and no failure escapes as an uncoded throw.
Enumeration output is deterministic across path separators and locale on Windows, macOS and Linux; ordering is canonical and a generated sweep asserts a non-zero case count.
No existing method's behaviour, signature, or refusal code changes; the pre-existing scope and artifact suites still pass unmodified except where a new capability is added to a frozen list.

New root value exports are transcribed into index-surface.test.ts's hand-written EXPECTED_EXPORTS with the count literal bumped, and fresh pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/runner test exits 0 with any residual red attributed to foreign paths against a recorded merge-base baseline.
taskRails: Additive enumeration only. Do not change, relax, or re-code any existing observer/store method or refusal code; a behaviour change here silently alters every scope observation and artifact receipt already in production.
These are external-effect boundaries: never invoke git through a shell, never accept a free-form command string, and keep every child bounded by maxBuffer, timeout and windowsHide.
A missing directory, an empty listing, and an unreadable entry are three different facts and must carry three different answers; an empty result is never proof of absence.
Tests assert the exact stable reason code and the refusing layer, and any generated sweep asserts it produced a non-zero number of cases.
Target <=250 physical lines per production file and split before 400; this cap is per file, not per task.

implementationPlan.description: TDD RED: add focused production-surface tests for createNodeGitObserver().listRefs() and createArtifactStore().enumerateArtifacts(). The Git matrix must cover real head/remote refs plus injected invalid UTF-8, truncated NUL fields/LF record termination, wrong field count, out-of-scope/duplicate ref, non-commit target, lowercase 40/64-hex validation, empty observation, generic/timeout failure, and both Node overflow shapes; every refusal asserts exact code and GIT_OBSERVER layer. The artifact matrix must cover real temp-store objects/staging, missing versus successful-empty versus unreadable listing/entry, unavailable optional FS capability, N/N+1 overflow, invalid/duplicate/non-file/symlink names, object-address mismatch, staging grammar, and permutation/path-separator/locale independence; assert exact code and ARTIFACT_FS_PORT or ARTIFACT_STORE layer. Hand-author case tables, assert each table length is >0, and assert exact generated/executed ID-set equality so a zero/filtered sweep cannot pass.
implementationPlan.note:
Fixed the three detached refusal cases QA named, plus one more of the same class QA did not flag. Test-only: `git hash-object` on scope-refs.ts, artifact-contract.ts and artifact-enumeration.ts each equals `git rev-parse HEAD:<path>`, so no production byte moved.

REPLACED FIXTURES (each new one is ACCEPTED once its named guard alone is neutered, which is what makes it go red):
1. invalid-utf8 -> invalid-utf8-inside-a-well-formed-record. Bytes `refs/heads/ma<0xff>in\0<COMMIT>\0commit\0\n` spliced by a new withRawByte() helper (no string literal can carry invalid UTF-8). Lenient decoding turns 0xff into U+FFFD, the name still starts with refs/heads/, the type is still `commit`, the target is still lowercase hex -> ACCEPTED. Only fatal decoding rejects it.
2. record-not-lf-terminated -> record-terminated-by-a-byte-other-than-lf. Bytes `refs/heads/main\0<COMMIT>\0commit\0X`: a COMPLETE four-field record whose LF was replaced. Neuter the LF guard and slice(0,-1) chops the X instead, four valid fields survive -> ACCEPTED. Only the LF guard rejects it. This is the exact acceptance hole QA measured.
3. uppercase-address (artifact). Now a synthetic listing returning name "A"x64 kind FILE whose readAll throws EACCES. The grammar refuses BEFORE any read, so widening it to [0-9a-fA-F] makes the entry an object candidate and the READ answers instead with a different code AND layer (RUNNER_ARTIFACT_VERIFY_FAILED/ARTIFACT_FS_PORT) -> red. Synthetic rather than on-disk so OS case folding cannot decide the case. I chose FIX, not delete.
4. FOUND BY ME, same class: truncated-field-count -> record-missing-its-trailing-nul, bytes `refs/heads/main\0<COMMIT>\0commit\n`. The old fixture dropped the TYPE field, so neutering the field-count guard left objectType === "" and the objecttype guard answered with the identical code and layer. The new one drops only the trailing NUL, so all three surviving fields are individually valid.

Checklist findings:
- Inputs: withRawByte() sizes the buffer as head+1+tail and writes the raw byte at head.length; 0xff is invalid UTF-8 in every position, so the fixture cannot become valid by accident. Empty/huge inputs unchanged (empty-observation and N+1-ceiling cases untouched).

The old fixture wrote "A"x64 to disk and trusted the OS to hand the name back unfolded; on a case-folding filesystem the case would have been decided by the platform, not by the grammar. Nothing is written to disk for it now.
- Side effects: the synthetic port's readAll throws on every call, and the only entry in the listing is the uppercase one, so no other assertion in that case depends on a read succeeding. Temp roots are still created per case by mkdtemp and removed in afterAll.
- Concurrency/TOCTOU: unchanged - each case owns a fresh mkdtemp root; no shared state added.
- Leak check: the case still asserts `result.message` does not contain the temp root; the refusal message names only the entry basename.
- Coverage not lost by the swap: an on-disk uppercase file would now duplicate unrecognised-entry-name (both die only under M10), which is the redundancy QA objected to.
- Case tables still hand-written and pinned: MALFORMED_CASES.length toBe(10), REFUSAL_CASES.length toBe(8), id-set uniqueness. No generated sweep was introduced.

Sizes: the two TEST files are 313 and 308 physical lines (from 281 and 294; the whole delta is comments explaining why each fixture is only rejectable by its own guard). Both under the 400 bar. QA REJECT — full evidence (qa_reject.reason is capped, this is the long form).

## What I verified GREEN — do not redo any of it

- Owned paths all present at HEAD (`git rev-parse --verify HEAD:<path>` per file, 13/13 OK), working tree clean over `packages/runner/src`. Work carried by 76012b8 (steps 1-5,7) + fbb2122 (step 6). No scratch/generated files in either.
- `pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck` exit 0; `pnpm --filter @moe/runner test` exit 0, **45 files / 1409 tests**, command unnarrowed (`vitest run --root ../.. packages/runner/src`).
- Repo-wide `pnpm typecheck` exit 0. Path-attributed baseline delta empty — no foreign red to attribute.
- DoD 1 GREEN: `listRefs()` goes through the existing `git()`/`runGit` boundary, fixed argv, shell:false, maxBuffer 8 MiB, 30s timeout, windowsHide. `git diff <merge-base>..HEAD -- scope-git.ts | grep hermetic` is EMPTY — `hermeticGitEnvironment` untouched.
- DoD 2 GREEN: `ArtifactFsPort.listDirectory?` optional, `ArtifactStore.enumerateArtifacts` required, `MAX_ARTIFACT_ENUMERATION_ENTRIES`. Nothing is skipped — unrecognised names refuse `RUNNER_ARTIFACT_ADDRESS_CORRUPT`.
- DoD 5 GREEN: additions are optional/additive; `withCause` leaves code+message byte-identical; `ScopeObserverError.layer` optional and third. `grep -rn ArtifactStore` outside `packages/runner/src` returns ZERO, so the newly-required store method breaks no external implementor. Repo typecheck confirms.
- DoD 6 GREEN: three runtime values published, count literal 147 -> 150, index.ts 275 lines (over the 250 target, under the 400 bar — per architect-705f0380's ruling in comment-ce31aae12773455aa06df017f436bddb this is explicitly NOT a rejection reason and I am not using it as one).
- Per-file cap: worst production file is index.ts 275, then scope-contract 259, scope-git 250. All under 400. Compliant.
- MY OWN mutation drills confirming two guards ARE pinned: neutering `digest !== entry.name` -> `× refuses object-bytes-do-not-match-address` (1 failed/15 passed). Neutering `objectType !== "commit"` -> `× refuses non-commit-target` (1 failed/20 passed). Both killed by exactly their named case.

## What FAILS — DoD 3 / epic rail 6 / project rail 1

Epic rail 6 states the protocol verbatim: "verify a failure-path test by mutating the production surface and confirming the test goes red." Three of this task's NEW refusal cases do not go red. Each mutation was applied one at a time, anchor count asserted == 1 before running, bytes backed up outside the repo, restored, and restoration verified by sha256 equality + empty `git diff`.

**(1) `record-not-lf-terminated` — scope-git.test.ts:141. REAL ACCEPTANCE HOLE.**
Mutation: `scope-refs.ts:47` `if (!text.endsWith("\n"))` -> `if (false && !text.endsWith("\n"))`. Anchor count 1. Result: **Tests 21 passed (21)**. Zero red.
Why: the fixture is `refs/heads/main\0<COMMIT>\0commit\0` with no LF. With the guard gone, `text.slice(0, -1)` chops the trailing NUL instead of an LF, the last record splits to 3 fields, and `fields.length !== 4` at scope-refs.ts:66 answers with the SAME code and SAME layer. The case is a duplicate of `truncated-field-count` and pins nothing.
The hole this masks: `refs/heads/main\0<COMMIT>\0commit\0X` (any trailing byte instead of LF) — chop removes `X`, four fields survive with `fields[3] === ""`, and the listing is **ACCEPTED**. The module docstring at scope-refs.ts:36-41 claims "the LF is part of the grammar and is validated rather than trimmed"; nothing tests that claim. No fixture in MALFORMED_CASES ends in a non-LF byte after a complete four-field record.

**(2) `invalid-utf8` — scope-git.test.ts:136. REAL ACCEPTANCE HOLE.**
Mutation: `scope-refs.ts:88` `{ fatal: true }` -> `{ fatal: false }`. Anchor count 1. Result: **Tests 21 passed (21)**. Zero red.
Why: fixture bytes `[0xff,0xfe,0x00,0x0a]` decode leniently to `��\0\n`, which splits to 2 fields and is caught by the same field-count guard with the same code. Fatal decoding is unpinned.
The hole this masks: a corrupt byte *inside an otherwise well-formed ref name* — `refs/heads/ma<0xff>in\0<COMMIT>\0commit\0\n` — decodes to `refs/heads/ma�in`, clears the scope check, the `commit` check and the hex check, and is **ACCEPTED**. The enumerator would then report a ref name that is not the one git emitted. No fixture puts invalid UTF-8 inside a name that would otherwise pass.

**(3) `uppercase-address` — artifact-enumeration.test.ts:200. Detached, but no reachable hole.**
Mutation: `artifact-contract.ts:175` `/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/u` -> `/^[0-9a-fA-F]{64}$/u`. Anchor count 1. Result: **Tests 16 passed (16)**. Zero red.
Why: with uppercase admitted, `"A".repeat(64)` becomes an object candidate and is then refused by the bytes-vs-address check with the identical code and layer. Lower severity than (1) and (2) — `sha256Hex` only ever emits lowercase, so no uppercase name can ever satisfy the digest check and there is no acceptance hole. Still a case that reads as covering the address grammar while measuring a different guard. Fix it or drop the redundant case, your call, but say which.

## What makes this pass

For (1) and (2): a fixture that the guard under test is the ONLY thing that can reject — i.e. one that is ACCEPTED once you neuter that guard. Then re-run the drill and show the named case going red. Same for (3) if you keep it. Note the step-7 note claims three drills all killed by their named case; those three were real (I reproduced two), but the LF-terminator and fatal-UTF-8 guards were never among them.

Nothing else is in dispute. This is a test-precision defect in two new test files, not a production defect — production refuses correctly today in every case I probed.
